name: doc-card-group
purpose: The framed, responsive grid a `DocCard` set sits in. The group is the frame, not each card: `RegistrationFrame` draws the perimeter and the four corner registration marks once around the whole set, the grid keeps 1px gaps, and every cell paints a 1px ring into them — so two neighbours share one hairline, an incomplete last row stays simply empty, and the set reads as one object the reader scans across rather than as loose tiles. `columns` names the widest column count; the grid always steps down toward one column on a phone unless a set of tiny cells opts into two with `mobileColumns`.
useWhen: Around every `DocCard` set — a card outside a group has no frame and no cell ring.
The fan-out at the top of a landing or section-index page: product tiles, a framework grid, a "what you can build" band.
avoidWhen: When each entry needs a full-measure sentence to be understood — use `DocItem` rows, one column, instead of cells.
As a general-purpose layout grid for application screens; it is documentation chrome, tied to the `DocProse` ladder.
related: `DocCard` — the cell this frames; the group draws the perimeter and the cells paint the internal rules.
`RegistrationFrame` — the layout primitive that draws the frame and the corner registration marks.
`DocProse` — the contract around it; `data-doc-block` puts the group on the block rung of the prose ladder.
bestPractices: Pick `columns` for the widest screen and let the breakpoints do the rest; do not wrap the group in another grid.
Leave `mobileColumns` at 1 unless every cell is a mark plus one word — a card with copy needs the whole phone width.
Let an incomplete last row be empty; do not stretch the last card to fill it.

Inside a `module` with `padded` off, place the group directly in the body: the header's bottom rule and the column's side rules become the group's top and sides, the group drops its own top and side rules and top corner marks, and the cells' rings land on those rules. The group's bottom rule closes the module, so the module after it passes `divided` as `false` — every seam stays one hairline.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Column count at the large breakpoint. A Markdown `CardGroup cols` attribute maps here (through DocMarkdown).

props.name: mobileColumns
props.doc: Column count on a phone. Two only pays when the cells are a mark plus a word.
